scope_rationale: problem.txt states the contract must hold for K that is not an exact multiple of group_size, with the trailing partial group being its own group.

evidence.summary: Each (K, group_size) case run in its own fresh CUDA process, eliminating context poisoning. K multiples of BLOCK_SIZE_K=16 are exact: K=64/gs32 max_abs 4.8e-6 (frac_off 0.0), K=48/gs32 max_abs 1.9e-6 (frac_off 0.0). K not a multiple of 16 is grossly wrong: K=40/gs32 max_abs 8.37 vs |ref|max 13.60 (rel 0.62, 99.9% of elements off >1e-3); K=72/gs32 max_abs 266.1 vs 16.13 (rel 16.5, 100% off); K=24/gs16 max_abs 12.39 vs 11.94 (rel 1.04, 100% off); K=56/gs32 max_abs 11.32 vs 14.45 (rel 0.78, 99.9% off). All of these are legal 4-bit packed shapes (K%8==0) with a trailing partial group. Confirms the unmasked K-loop (num_pid_k = cdiv(K,16), no k-range mask on a/b/g_idx loads) corrupts the accumulator for K not divisible by BLOCK_SIZE_K.

rationale: num_pid_k = cdiv(K, 16) but the loads of a (masked only on M), b, and g_ptrs have no K-range mask, so the final iteration processes columns k >= K with garbage data added into the accumulator.

scope_evidence.summary: 'Contract: ... for any K -- including a K that is not an exact multiple of group_size, where the trailing partial group is still a group of its own.' The kernel wrapper docstring declares b_packed shape (K//(32//bits), N), which K=40 satisfies.

scope_rationale: problem.txt says the contract holds 'for any K'; K=40 is representable in the declared packed layout (b_packed has K//8 = 5 int32 rows) and yields a partial trailing group with group_size=32.
statement: For K not a multiple of BLOCK_SIZE_K=16 (e.g. K=40 with group_size=32, a legal 4-bit-packed shape since 40 % 8 == 0), the kernel's unmasked K-loop reads A, B and g_idx past the end of the tensors and produces results that differ materially from the reference (or faults).
